Thank you, Mr. Chair. In particular, microgravity provides conditions that cannot be replicated on Earth, in which may enable advances in biomedical research and pharmaceutical development that could ultimately benefit patients worldwide. The United Kingdom recognizes the growing scientific evidence that microgravity can support more precise formulation and characterization of complex medicines, including biologics and protein-based therapeutics. Research conducted in microgravity has demonstrated potential improvements in areas such as crystallization, purity, stability, and solubility, which are critical factors in the safety, efficacy, and accessibility of medicines. The United Kingdom considers that these opportunities may be especially relevant for conditions such as rare diseases, precision oncology, and the development of medicines that must remain stable in remote or resource-constrained settings. At the same time, the United Kingdom recognizes that the realization of these opportunities depends on addressing a set of shared and interconnected challenges. These include reliable and affordable access to orbit, safe and predictable return capabilities, integration with terrestrial supply chains, and the availability of clear, proportionate, and internationally coherent regulatory approaches. Without progress in these areas, the translation of space-based research into real-world health benefits will remain limited. The United Kingdom emphasizes that with the knowledge, evidence, and outcomes arising from this research should widely be accessible and contribute to global health advancement, including for member states without direct access to orbital infrastructure. The United Kingdom believes that regulatory clarity is a key enabler of responsible innovation and in-orbit pharmaceutical manufacturing. As space enabled biomedical research and manufacturing mature, there is a growing need to clarify how existing regulatory frameworks for medicines, medical products, and space activities can be applied to novel end-to-end pathways spanning both Earth and space. The UK considers early engagement between regulators, scientists, healthcare stakeholders, and industry essential to enabling safe experimentation, supporting validation and trials, maintaining public trust, and providing the clarity needed for sustained research, development, and responsible commercial participation. In this context, the United Kingdom is undertaking exploratory work to provide greater regulatory clarity for space-enabled pharmaceutical research and manufacturing. focused on evidence building and practical guidance rather than rule setting. This approach aims to reduce uncertainty, support safe and effective development pathways, and inform future international dialogue toward globally compatible regulatory practices as the field evolves with the evidence and lessons generated contributing to wider international learning on how space enabled health innovations may be developed safely and responsively for the benefit of all. Space-enabled health innovations must therefore be designed with clear pathways for validation, adoption, and integration into existing healthcare systems. The United Kingdom further recognizes that no single nation can realize the full potential of these developments alone. International cooperation is essential to maximize the benefits of microgravity research for global health, avoid fragmentation of standards, and ensure that advances are shared in line with the principles of the peaceful uses of outer space. Collaborative research, knowledge exchange, and dialogue on regulatory and ethical considerations will be particularly important as capabilities continue to evolve. The United Kingdom considers COPUOS to be a valuable forum for supporting such dialogue and shared learning. In closing, the United Kingdom encourages Member States to consider how COPUOS and its subcommittees can continue to support discussion on the health applications of space science, including emerging areas such as space-enabled pharmaceutical research and manufacturing. A coordinated, inclusive, and forward-looking approach grounded in shared learning and mutual benefit will help ensure these developments are realized safely, responsibly, and for the benefit of all humanity. Thank you, Mr. Chair.
